summary: Implementable specs for the Volatility agent family (5 leaf agents under a `volatility` branch in quant/agents/volatility.py, all subclassing QuantAgent from /Users/mac/Downloads/div_4_doc/Trading_project_2.0/quant/base.py). india_vix maps the live India VIX quote onto India-calibrated regime bands (<11 complacent, 11-14 calm, 14-18 normal, 18-24 elevated, 24-32 fear, >32 panic) with piecewise-linear scoring plus a VIX day-change adjustment; iv_level inverts ATM monthly-option premiums to IV (existing mathutils.implied_vol), scores via IV percentile from a self-recorded rolling daily store (data/iv_store.json, 252-day window) and bootstraps day one with absolute Indian single-stock IV bands blended in until 60 days of history; iv_skew measures 5%-OTM (25-delta proxy) put-minus-call IV normalized by ATM IV, with steepening detection off the same store; vega_env ships as an honest disabled-by-default stub (vega is irrelevant to cash-stock P&L; vomma/veta are computable point-in-time but unscoreable without vol-of-vol history — it only flags vol-crush risk for option execution); event reads a user-maintained data/events.json and applies proximity-decayed penalties within 3 days of market/stock events, skipping (None) when the file is absent. All agents return (None, reason) on missing chain/VIX data per the tree's skip semantics, need one shared pw_linear interpolation helper in mathutils, and share atm_iv/ivp via ctx.meta so the chain is inverted once per signal (<1s from the cached ChainSnapshot).

algorithms.name: India VIX Regime
algorithms.inputs: ctx.vix (India VIX last price, float); optional vix_pc = percent change vs previous close from the VIX GetQuotes response field 'pc' (requires a one-line DataHub extension, see data_requirements); ctx.direction.
algorithms.params: ANCHORS_BUY = [(9,70),(11,85),(13,90),(15,82),(17,70),(20,52),(24,38),(30,20),(40,8)]; ANCHORS_SELL = [(9,60),(11,70),(13,78),(15,82),(17,80),(20,68),(24,55),(30,38),(40,20)]; DAYCHG_COEF_BUY = -1.5, DAYCHG_CLAMP_BUY = (-15,+10); DAYCHG_COEF_SELL = +1.0, DAYCHG_CLAMP_SELL = (-10,+10). Regime labels for the detail string: <11 complacent, 11-14 calm, 14-18 normal, 18-24 elevated, 24-32 fear, >32 panic (India-calibrated: post-2015 VIX mostly 10-20, median ~14-15, >20 elevated caution, >30 extreme; 2008 ~92, Mar-2020 ~87, Jun-2024 election ~27).
algorithms.steps:
1. v = ctx.vix. If v is None or v <= 0: return (None, 'India VIX unavailable').
2. Add helper to quant/mathutils.py: pw_linear(x, pts) — pts is a sorted list of (x_i, y_i); if x <= pts[0][0] return pts[0][1]; if x >= pts[-1][0] return pts[-1][1]; else linearly interpolate between the bracketing pair. (Shared by all agents in this family.)
3. base = pw_linear(v, ANCHORS_BUY) if ctx.direction == BUY else pw_linear(v, ANCHORS_SELL).
4. Day-change adjustment (optional): fetch pc = VIX percent change. If available: adj = clamp(COEF_dir * pc, *CLAMP_dir); else adj = 0. Rationale: VIX rising intraday = vol expanding = dips keep extending (bad for mean-reversion BUY, mildly good for SELL); VIX falling = vol crush = reversion-friendly.
5. score = clamp(base + adj, 0, 100).
6. detail = f'VIX {v:.2f} ({regime_label}), day chg {pc:+.1f}%' (omit chg if unavailable).
7. Return (score, detail). Cost: one cached quote, no chain fetch — microseconds.
algorithms.buy_score_logic: score = clamp(pw_linear(vix, ANCHORS_BUY) + clamp(-1.5*vix_pc, -15, +10), 0, 100). Peak 90 at VIX~13 (calm regime: pullbacks in uptrends revert reliably); ~70 at 17; 52 at 20; 38 at 24; <=20 above 30. Rationale: dip-buying a stock when index vol is elevated means fat left tails — the RSI/W%R dip is more often the start of a leg down than a spring; complacent VIX <11 gets a mild haircut (70-85) because vol expansion risk is asymmetric from the floor.
algorithms.sell_score_logic: score = clamp(pw_linear(vix, ANCHORS_SELL) + clamp(+1.0*vix_pc, -10, +10), 0, 100). Peak ~82 at VIX 15-17 and stays >=55 up to 24: shorting rips in a Supertrend downtrend is with-the-flow when vol is elevated (vol clusters with downtrends). Penalized at both ends: <11 (grinding low-vol tape, tops keep extending, 60-70) and >30 (panic regime: violent short-covering rallies, gap/circuit risk, <=38).
algorithms.default_weight: buy 1.0, sell 1.0 — market-wide regime context that applies to every stock signal equally; strong enough to matter but it should not outvote stock-specific agents.
algorithms.data_requirements: Uses DataHub.india_vix() (NSE GetQuotes on the INDIA VIX token already resolved in _find_vix_token). For the day-change adjustment, extend DataHub with india_vix_quote() returning the full quote dict so 'pc' is readable (touchline/GetQuotes both carry pc); if only lp is exposed, skip step 4 silently. If the VIX token was not found in the scrip master, return (None, ...) and the tree skips this agent.

algorithms.name: ATM IV Level (percentile with absolute-band bootstrap)
algorithms.inputs: ctx.chain (ChainSnapshot: spot, expiry_epoch, strikes with CE/PE ltp/oi/volume), ctx.now; rolling per-symbol daily ATM IV store at /Users/mac/Downloads/div_4_doc/Trading_project_2.0/data/iv_store.json; ctx.direction; writes ctx.meta['atm_iv'] and ctx.meta['ivp'] for sibling agents.
algorithms.params: MIN_T_YEARS = 2/365 (skip inside last 2 days of the monthly expiry — IV inversion too noisy); IV_SANITY = (0.05, 3.00); ABS_TO_PCTL anchors (annualized IV -> pseudo-percentile) = [(0.12,5),(0.18,15),(0.25,35),(0.32,55),(0.42,75),(0.60,92),(0.80,99)] (Indian F&O single stocks: large caps typically 15-30% IV, midcaps 30-50%, >60% = event/results pricing); SCORE_BUY anchors on percentile p = [(0,55),(20,80),(40,95),(55,85),(70,60),(85,38),(100,15)]; SCORE_SELL = [(0,50),(20,70),(40,85),(55,88),(70,72),(85,52),(100,25)]; MIN_HIST = 20 records before empirical percentile is used; FULL_HIST = 60 (blend weight w = min(1, n/60)); PCTL_WINDOW = 252 most recent stored days (standard IV-percentile lookback; percentile preferred over IV rank because rank is distorted by one spike); STORE_CAP = 400 dates/symbol.
algorithms.steps:
1. chain = ctx.chain; if None: return (None, 'option chain unavailable'). t = years_to_expiry(chain.expiry_epoch, ctx.now); if t < MIN_T_YEARS: return (None, 'monthly expiry too close for stable IV').
2. chain.compute_ivs() (idempotent — legs with iv already set are skipped).
3. ATM IV: k = chain.atm_strike(); row = its StrikeRow. ivs = [leg.iv for leg in (row.ce, row.pe) if leg and leg.iv]. If empty, scan strike rows at index atm±1 then atm±2 (nearest-first) and take the first row yielding any valid iv; average available CE/PE ivs of that row. If still empty: return (None, 'no invertible ATM premium'). atm_iv = mean(ivs); if not IV_SANITY[0] <= atm_iv <= IV_SANITY[1]: return (None, f'ATM IV {atm_iv:.2f} out of sanity range').
4. Store I/O (implement a small IVStore class, shared with iv_skew): load JSON {symbol: {"YYYY-MM-DD": {"iv": float, "skew": float|null}}} once per process with a 60s mtime cache; upsert store[symbol][today_ist]["iv"] = round(atm_iv, 4) (last write of the day wins — one record per trading day); prune to newest STORE_CAP dates; atomic save (write .tmp then os.replace). today_ist from zoneinfo('Asia/Kolkata').
5. hist = up to PCTL_WINDOW most recent stored iv values for symbol EXCLUDING today. n = len(hist).
6. p_abs = pw_linear(atm_iv, ABS_TO_PCTL). If n >= MIN_HIST: p_emp = 100 * count(h < atm_iv for h in hist) / n; w = min(1.0, n / FULL_HIST); p = w*p_emp + (1-w)*p_abs. Else: p = p_abs (day-one bootstrap).
7. score = pw_linear(p, SCORE_BUY or SCORE_SELL per ctx.direction).
8. ctx.meta['atm_iv'] = atm_iv; ctx.meta['ivp'] = p; ctx.meta['atm_strike'] = k (siblings reuse — chain is inverted once per signal).
9. detail = f'ATM IV {atm_iv*100:.1f}%, pctl {p:.0f} ({n}d hist{", bootstrap" if n < MIN_HIST else ""})'. Return (score, detail).
algorithms.buy_score_logic: score = pw_linear(p, [(0,55),(20,80),(40,95),(55,85),(70,60),(85,38),(100,15)]) where p is blended IV percentile. Peak 95 at p~40: mid-range vol is the mean-reversion sweet spot. p>=70 penalized hard (60 -> 15): rich IV on a single stock usually means the market is pricing an event (results, news) — the dip can be information, not noise, and a long entry eats the realized move. p<=20 mildly penalized (55-80): rock-bottom IV precedes expansion and the dip may be the first crack.
algorithms.sell_score_logic: score = pw_linear(p, [(0,50),(20,70),(40,85),(55,88),(70,72),(85,52),(100,25)]). Peak 88 at p~55 — shorting a rip tolerates somewhat richer vol than dip-buying (elevated stock IV often accompanies distribution/downtrends), but extreme p>=85 still penalized: it flags binary event risk and violent squeeze potential in both directions.
algorithms.default_weight: buy 1.0, sell 1.0 — the core stock-specific volatility read; equal footing with india_vix.
algorithms.data_requirements: DataHub.chain_snapshot() (GetOptionChain window of ATM±8 strikes + GetQuotes per strike, 90s TTL cache) plus existing mathutils.implied_vol/years_to_expiry. No IV history exists anywhere in Shoonya, so the agent records its own: data/iv_store.json grows one record per symbol per trading day the scanner evaluates it; percentile activates at 20 records and fully replaces the absolute bands at 60. If the chain is missing/illiquid or expiry is <2 days out, return None (agent skipped, weight redistributed by the tree).

algorithms.name: IV Skew (put-call skew, 25-delta proxy)
algorithms.inputs: ctx.chain with per-leg IVs (reuses ctx.meta['atm_iv'] / ['atm_strike'] if iv_level already ran, else computes them identically); the same data/iv_store.json for daily skew history; ctx.direction.
algorithms.params: OTM_MONEYNESS m = 0.05 (5% OTM — for a typical stock IV ~30% and monthly T~0.06y, 1 sigma ≈ 7.3%, so 5% OTM ≈ 0.7 sigma ≈ the 25-delta zone without needing delta math); leg liquidity filter: iv is not None AND ltp > 0 AND (oi > 0 OR volume > 0); fallback ladder: 5%-OTM pair -> pair 2 strike-indices from ATM -> pair 1 index from ATM -> ATM-only PE-CE skew; SCORE_BUY anchors on r = [(-0.15,80),(-0.08,88),(0,82),(0.05,72),(0.10,55),(0.18,35),(0.30,18)]; SCORE_SELL = [(-0.15,30),(-0.08,45),(0,62),(0.05,75),(0.10,85),(0.18,78),(0.30,60)]; steepening: baseline = median of last 5 stored daily skews (need >= 3), ADJ_BUY = clamp(-250*d, -15, +8), ADJ_SELL = clamp(+250*d, -8, +12) where d = r_today - baseline.
algorithms.steps:
1. chain = ctx.chain; if None: return (None, 'option chain unavailable'). Ensure compute_ivs() ran; get atm_iv (from ctx.meta or recompute as in iv_level steps 1-3); if atm_iv unavailable: return (None, 'no ATM IV').
2. Candidate put leg: among strike rows with strike < atm_strike, pick the row minimizing |strike - spot*(1-m)| whose PE passes the liquidity filter; candidate call: among rows with strike > atm_strike, minimize |strike - spot*(1+m)| with liquid CE.
3. If either side failed, walk the fallback ladder: symmetric pair at ATM index ±2, then ±1 (both legs must pass the filter), finally the ATM row's own PE/CE (mark detail 'ATM skew only'). If no pair works: return (None, 'chain too illiquid for skew').
4. r = (put_iv - call_iv) / atm_iv  — relative skew, comparable across a 300-rupee midcap and a 4000-rupee large cap. (Raw put_iv - call_iv in vol points goes in the detail string.)
5. base = pw_linear(r, SCORE_BUY or SCORE_SELL per direction).
6. Steepening adjustment: read last 5 stored daily skew values for symbol (excluding today) from iv_store; if >= 3 exist: d = r - median(them); adj = ADJ_dir(d); else adj = 0. Upsert store[symbol][today]["skew"] = round(r, 4) (same IVStore instance/atomic write as iv_level).
7. score = clamp(base + adj, 0, 100). detail = f'rel skew {r:+.3f} (put {put_iv*100:.1f}% @ {kp} / call {call_iv*100:.1f}% @ {kc}), 5d chg {d:+.3f}'.
8. Return (score, detail).
algorithms.buy_score_logic: score = clamp(pw_linear(r, [(-0.15,80),(-0.08,88),(0,82),(0.05,72),(0.10,55),(0.18,35),(0.30,18)]) + clamp(-250*(r - median5d), -15, +8), 0, 100). Steep put skew (r >= 0.10: puts bid >=10% of ATM IV over calls) means the market is paying up for downside protection on this stock — dip-buying into institutional hedging demand is penalized to 55 and below; a skew that STEEPENED vs its own 5-day median is penalized further (up to -15) because fresh put demand often front-runs continuation. Flat-to-call skew (r <= 0) supports the dip (82-88).
algorithms.sell_score_logic: score = clamp(pw_linear(r, [(-0.15,30),(-0.08,45),(0,62),(0.05,75),(0.10,85),(0.18,78),(0.30,60)]) + clamp(+250*(r - median5d), -8, +12), 0, 100). Put skew steep and steepening = smart-money downside positioning = supports shorting the rip (peak 85 near r=0.10). Inverted skew (calls over puts, r <= -0.08) = speculative call-buying frenzy — shorting into that risks a gamma squeeze, scored 30-45. Extreme panic skew r >= 0.25 pulled back to 60: puts that stretched tend to mark capitulation, and the bounce/vol-crush hurts fresh shorts.
algorithms.default_weight: buy 0.8, sell 0.8 — single-stock skew from 8-strike monthly chains with wide spreads is noisier than VIX or ATM IV level; useful confirmation, not a driver.
algorithms.data_requirements: Same ChainSnapshot as iv_level (zero extra API calls when evaluated in the same signal — legs and IVs are already cached; enforce evaluation order iv_level before iv_skew in registry.py, or let each lazily compute). Needs the shared IVStore for the steepening baseline; without >=3 days of stored skew the adjustment is skipped and only the level score applies. Illiquid chains (no leg pair passes the filter) return None.

algorithms.name: Vega Environment (vomma/veta future stub)
algorithms.inputs: ctx.chain (ATM CE/PE ltp for straddle), ctx.meta['atm_iv'] and ctx.meta['ivp'] from iv_level (recompute if absent), years_to_expiry, mathutils.bs_vega.
algorithms.params: default_enabled = False (ships as a disabled future stub per the base.py convention); HIGH_VEGA_T = 12/365 (vega meaningful only with >=12 days to expiry; below 5/365 it is a gamma environment, not vega); HIGH_IVP = 70, LOW_IVP = 30; scores: crush-risk case 30, cheap-vega case 65, otherwise 50 (both directions).
algorithms.steps:
HONEST ASSESSMENT (state this in the class docstring): the trade signal executes on the CASH stock, so vega/vomma/veta do not touch the position's P&L at all — they only matter if the user chooses to express the signal via options. Beyond that, higher-order vol greeks are genuinely out of reach with Shoonya data: vomma = vega*d1*d2/sigma and veta are computable POINT-IN-TIME from BS, but scoring them requires a vol-of-vol history or a multi-expiry surface (term structure), and we have one monthly expiry, no IV history except what iv_store accumulates, and no intraday IV ticks. Any 'vomma score' would be numerology. Therefore: minimal useful version = a flag for vol-crush risk relevant to OPTION execution, disabled by default.
1. chain = ctx.chain; if None: return (None, 'option chain unavailable').
2. t = years_to_expiry(chain.expiry_epoch, ctx.now); atm_iv, ivp = ctx.meta.get('atm_iv'), ctx.meta.get('ivp') (compute via iv_level's steps 1-6 if missing; if still None return (None, 'no ATM IV')).
3. straddle_pct = (atm_ce.ltp + atm_pe.ltp)/chain.spot*100 if both ATM legs have ltp else None — the implied move to expiry, for the detail string.
4. vega_1pct = bs_vega(chain.spot, atm_strike, t, atm_iv) * 0.01 — rupees per option per 1 vol-point, detail only.
5. Classification: high_vega_env = (t >= HIGH_VEGA_T). If high_vega_env and ivp >= HIGH_IVP: score = 30 ('rich IV + high vega: long-option execution eats vol crush'). Elif high_vega_env and ivp <= LOW_IVP: score = 65 ('cheap vega: long-option execution favourable'). Else score = 50 (neutral).
6. detail = f'vega env: T={t*365:.0f}d, IVpctl {ivp:.0f}, straddle {straddle_pct:.1f}% move, vega {vega_1pct:.2f}/pt; vomma/veta not scored (no vol-of-vol data)'.
7. Return (score, detail). FUTURE: once iv_store holds 120+ days per symbol, a real vol-of-vol input exists (stdev of daily IV changes) and this stub can score vomma exposure properly.
algorithms.buy_score_logic: Identical map both directions (the flag is about execution vehicle, not direction): 30 if T>=12d and IV percentile>=70 (buying calls here pays peak vega on rich vol); 65 if T>=12d and percentile<=30; else 50. Deliberately compressed around neutral so it cannot swing the tree even when enabled.
algorithms.sell_score_logic: Same as buy: 30 / 65 / 50 on the same conditions — vol-crush risk when buying puts to express the SELL is symmetric.
algorithms.default_weight: buy 0.3, sell 0.3, default_enabled=False — honest stub: near-zero information for cash-stock execution; enable only if signals are executed via long options.
algorithms.data_requirements: Reuses the cached ChainSnapshot and iv_level's ctx.meta outputs; mathutils.bs_vega already exists. No new endpoints. Unavailable chain or IV -> None (skipped). Explicitly NOT required/possible from Shoonya: IV tick history, multi-expiry surface, variance futures — which is why vomma/veta stay unscored.

algorithms.name: Event Proximity (manual calendar stub)
algorithms.inputs: User-maintained file /Users/mac/Downloads/div_4_doc/Trading_project_2.0/data/events.json; ctx.symbol; today's date in Asia/Kolkata. No API data.
algorithms.params: File schema: {"events": [{"date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "name": "RBI policy", "scope": "market"|"<SYMBOL>", "severity": "high"|"medium"|"low"}]}. N_BEFORE = 3 calendar days; BASE_PENALTY = {high: 60, medium: 35, low: 15}; PROXIMITY = {0: 1.0, 1: 0.8, 2: 0.6, 3: 0.4}; DAY_AFTER = 0.5 proximity for days_until == -1, applied ONLY to stock-scope high/medium events (results announced yesterday still gap/whipsaw today); MARKET_SCOPE_FACTOR = 0.8 (budget/RBI/Fed hit single stocks slightly less than the named stock's own results); file re-read with 60s mtime cache. Seed file for the user: budget day, RBI MPC dates, monthly F&O expiry (optional, severity low, scope market), per-stock results dates.
algorithms.steps:
1. Load data/events.json (60s mtime cache; tolerant parser — skip malformed entries, log once). If the file does not exist or parses to no list: return (None, 'events.json not found — event agent skipped'). Rationale: absence of a calendar is absence of knowledge; None makes the tree redistribute weight instead of fabricating a 100.
2. today = date in zoneinfo('Asia/Kolkata'). For each event: d = (event.date - today).days; sym_match = (scope == 'market') or (scope.upper() == ctx.symbol.upper()). Keep events where sym_match and (0 <= d <= N_BEFORE or (d == -1 and scope != 'market' and severity in ('high','medium'))).
3. For each kept event: penalty = BASE_PENALTY[severity] * (PROXIMITY[d] if d >= 0 else DAY_AFTER) * (MARKET_SCOPE_FACTOR if scope == 'market' else 1.0).
4. total = max(penalties) if any else 0 — take the single worst event, do NOT sum (a budget day plus results day is not 120 points of badness, it is one no-trade day).
5. score = clamp(100 - total, 0, 100). Same for BUY and SELL — pre-event gap risk is directionless for a mean-reversion entry.
6. detail = 'no events within 3d' or f'{event.name} ({scope}, {severity}) in {d}d -> -{total:.0f}'.
7. Return (score, detail). Worked examples: stock results tomorrow (high, d=1): 100 - 60*0.8 = 52. RBI policy today (high, market): 100 - 60*1.0*0.8 = 52. Results were yesterday (high, stock, d=-1): 100 - 60*0.5 = 70. Low-severity expiry day in 2 days: 100 - 15*0.6*0.8 = 92.8.
algorithms.buy_score_logic: score = clamp(100 - max_over_matching_events(BASE_PENALTY[severity] * proximity_factor(days_until) * scope_factor), 0, 100). 100 when no event is within the window; a high-severity event on the day itself drives the score to 40-52, which drags the volatility branch enough to veto marginal entries while letting very strong multi-agent signals through.
algorithms.sell_score_logic: Identical formula and parameters as BUY — a binary event (results, RBI, budget) invalidates the mean-reversion edge in both directions; there is no directional information in a calendar date.
algorithms.default_weight: buy 1.2, sell 1.2 — when the user HAS entered a date, it is high-conviction information and should outweigh the statistical agents; when the file is absent the agent returns None and the weight is harmlessly redistributed.
algorithms.data_requirements: No Shoonya endpoint — Shoonya provides no corporate-action/economic calendar, hence the manual stub. Requires only data/events.json maintained by the user (results dates from NSE announcements, RBI MPC calendar, Union Budget). Missing file or empty list -> (None, ...) so the agent is skipped, per the tree's skip semantics. FUTURE upgrade path: replace the file-reader internals with an NSE-announcements scraper without touching scoring.

notes: Implementation wiring for the developer: (1) put all five classes in /Users/mac/Downloads/div_4_doc/Trading_project_2.0/quant/agents/volatility.py under a VolatilityBranch(QuantAgent) with key 'volatility' and register it in registry.py; (2) add pw_linear(x, points) to quant/mathutils.py — every score table above is piecewise-linear interpolation over the listed anchors, clamped at the ends; (3) build one IVStore class (JSON at data/iv_store.json, per-symbol per-IST-date records {iv, skew}, 60s mtime cache, atomic tmp+os.replace writes, 400-date cap) shared by iv_level and iv_skew; (4) evaluation order iv_level -> iv_skew -> vega_env so ctx.meta['atm_iv'/'ivp'/'atm_strike'] is computed once from the 90s-TTL ChainSnapshot — total marginal cost of the family is one VIX quote plus the chain snapshot the tree already fetches, well under 1s; (5) DataHub needs one tiny extension: expose the VIX quote's 'pc' field (india_vix_quote()) for the day-change adjustment, which degrades gracefully if absent. India-specific calibration notes: VIX bands were set for the post-2015 Indian regime (mostly 10-20, all-time lows ~10 in 2023-24, >20 elevated, >30 extreme — spikes: 2008 ~92, Mar-2020 ~87, Jun-2024 election ~27); several retail-education sources still quote '15-30 normal', which reflects the pre-2015 era and would mis-score today's tape, so the bands deliberately sit lower. IV percentile (% of past days below current, 252-day window) was chosen over IV rank because a single results-day spike distorts rank for a year; the 20-record activation / 60-record full-weight blend against absolute Indian single-stock bands (large caps ~15-30% IV, midcaps 30-50%, >60% event pricing) gives sane day-one behavior. Sources: Finnovate India VIX 2026 (https://www.finnovate.in/learn/blog/india-vix-2026-what-fear-index-tells-investors), Bajaj AMC India VIX guide (https://www.bajajamc.com/knowledge-centre/india-vix-index), Sahi India VIX explained (https://www.sahi.com/blogs/india-vix-volatility-index-explained), NiftyTrader VIX zones (https://www.niftytrader.in/markets/when-fear-stops-rising-markets-start-stabilizing/), Barchart IV rank vs percentile (https://www.barchart.com/education/iv_rank_vs_iv_percentile), Schwab IV percentiles (https://www.schwab.com/learn/story/using-implied-volatility-percentiles), SlashTraders IVR vs IVP (https://slashtraders.com/en/blog/iv-rank-vs-iv-percentile/).
